label: lem:zero_deriv_constant
title: Zero derivative implies constant
statement: Let $G : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a,b]$ and satisfy $\texttt{HasDerivAt}\; G\; 0\; x$ for all $x \in (a,b)$. Then $G(x) = G(a)$ for all $x \in [a,b]$.
proof: By the Mean Value Theorem (Lemma~\ref{lem:mean_value_theorem}), for any $x \in [a,b]$ with $a < x$, there exists $c \in (a,x)$ such that $G'(c) = (G(x) - G(a))/(x - a)$. Since $G'(c) = 0$, we get $G(x) = G(a)$.
